title: Double `+ - *`: IEEE, NaN for `inf - inf` and `0 * inf`
verdict: IEEE: NaN where the reference raises
description: Double arithmetic is IEEE 754: `inf - inf`, `inf + (-inf)` and `0 * inf` are NaN. Every other edge case agrees with the reference.

An operation on finite values whose result overflows gives `±inf` without raising, in `Float64` and in `Float32`: `1e308 + 1e308` and `1e308 * 10` are inf, `-1e308 - 1e308` is -inf; `Float32` overflows at its own range (`3e38 + 3e38` is inf). Same on both engines.

A literal `±0.0` addend or subtrahend returns the column unchanged, and `0.0 - x` is `-x` (the literal kernels' shortcuts, float.rs#L45-L65): `-0.0 + 0.0` is -0.0 and `0.0 - 0.0` is -0.0, where IEEE gives +0.0. Two columns give +0.0, and so does a one-row morsel of the streaming engine (polars-zero-sign-streaming). The NaN cases above are unaffected.
No upstream test pins `inf - inf`, `inf + (-inf)`, `0 * inf` or the `±0.0` shortcuts; they may change between versions.
reference: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply` raise a domain issue for `inf - inf` and `0 · inf` (`nan_creation`: raise, #257).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: The same section at tag py-2.1.0.

provenance.notes: Polars's user guide says it generally follows IEEE 754 for `Float32` and `Float64`, with two exceptions: any NaN equals any other NaN and is greater than every non-NaN value, and operations guarantee nothing about the sign of zero or NaN or a NaN's payload (a sort or group by may make every zero +0 and every NaN a positive NaN). It promises no error bound unless a function says otherwise. The user guide is not versioned; the section reads the same at tag py-2.1.0. So `inf - inf` and `0 * inf` are NaN in `Float32` as in `Float64` (IEEE 754's invalid operation). Settles the `Float32` row at docs level; the probes cover `Float64`.

notes: `impl_float_arith_kernel!` is one macro instantiated for `pf16`, `f32` and `f64`, so `Float32` and `Float64` run the same operations. The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (`StreamExpr` in crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so it shares these kernels with the in-memory engine. `+ - *` are the IEEE operations, so `inf - inf` and `0 * inf` are NaN in `Float32` as in `Float64`. The literal shortcuts (`x + 0`, `x * 1`) return `x`, which changes no NaN.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

evidence.note: lf = pl.LazyFrame({'a': [big, -big], 'b': [big, big], 'c': [10.0, small]}) with all three Float64 (big 1e308, small 1e-10) and Float32 (big 3e38, small 1e-3); select a + b, a - b, a * c, a / c; pl.LazyFrame(...).collect(engine=e) for e in ('in-memory', 'streaming'), polars 2.1.0 → Float64: [(inf, 0.0, inf, 1e+307), (0.0, -inf, -1.0000000000000001e+298, -inf)]; Float32: [(inf, 0.0, inf, 3.000000106909804e+37), (0.0, -inf, -3.0000001227554363e+35, -inf)]; streaming the same
a ±0 literal addend or subtrahend returns lhs unchanged, and 0 - x is neg(x): -0.0 + 0.0 and 0.0 - 0.0 give -0.0 (IEEE: +0.0)

provenance.notes: Added to the description: the ±0 literal shortcuts (`-0.0 + 0.0` is -0.0), which polars-zero-sign-streaming recorded and this fact lacked.
